messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy is unlikely to vanish entirely, though data collection, surveillance, and platform sharing are expanding, so total loss of privacy is remote and partial erosion is more probable Privacy
Consciousness copying to a computer by the early 2030s is far more speculative than digital backup, because identity, memory, embodiment, and subjective experience remain unresolved, so a full transfer is unlikely Consciousness
Wireless Internet available anywhere on planet is improbable soon, because terrain, power, economics, and last-mile access persist, though satellite networks may greatly extend coverage, so global but not everywhere coverage is plausible Wireless
Transport becoming fully electric for all forms is plausible over a very long time for cars, but aviation, shipping, rail, and heavy industry face energy density and infrastructure barriers, so eventual electrification is possible but slow Transport
Climate change effects include some irreversible outcomes on human timescales, such as warming, sea-level rise, ice loss, and ecosystem collapse, so the prediction is highly likely in part but too broad if it means every effect Climate
Money in physical coins and notes is less likely to vanish completely than to decline, because cash supports privacy, resilience, and inclusion, though digital payments may make it marginal in many rich economies Money
Genetic secrets for living centuries or forever are extremely speculative, because aging, cancer, repair, and societal limits are deep problems, so meaningful life extension is plausible but radical immortality is very unlikely Genetics
